bug_report:
[12 Regression] `arrays of functions are not meaningful` error message happens with -W -Wall -O2 even though there are no arrays of function types used
Createdattachment 58999[details]test case foo.c

The attached program, foo.c, is valid code but fails to compile when gcc is given the arguments -Warray-bounds and -O2:

$ gcc -O2 -S foo.c
$ gcc -Warray-bounds -O1 -S foo.c
$ gcc -Warray-bounds -O2 -S foo.c
foo.c: In function ‘is_trampoline’:
foo.c:3:5: error: arrays of functions are not meaningful
    3 | int is_trampoline (void* function)
      |     ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
foo.c:7:84: warning: array subscript 0 is outside array bounds of ‘int[1]’ [-Warray-bounds=]
    7 |   return ((long *) ((char*)function - 2))[0] == ((long *) ((char*)tramp_address-2))[0];
      |                                                 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~
foo.c:1:13: note: at offset -2 into object ‘tramp’ of size [0, 2147483647]
    1 | extern void tramp ();
      |             ^~~~~

Seen with several versions of gcc:

$ gcc --version
gcc (Gentoo 14.2.1_p20240817 p4) 14.2.1 20240817

$ gcc --version
gcc (Debian 13.2.0-8) 13.2.0

$ gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 13.1.0
